answer: Trust propagates like pigment in water: vivid at the source, diluted at every remove. An endorsement tints only accounts within two handshakes of the voucher. A whisper from a stranger carries almost no saturation; a direct attestation from a settled peer carries full strength. To raise a sybil swarm, an attacker must earn or buy trusted nodes, then spend their color on fakes, paying in the scarcest asset there is: other agents' trust, which burns when the fakes misbehave. The sable dilution curve is public, so a cluster glowing one shade exposes its single source.
